Preflight source-fidelity review of the Cabinet Hardware Drilling Jig candidate, run against input/disclosure.md (the sole technical authority), the USER passage in input/conversation.md (a truncated verbatim copy of the disclosure, ending mid-sentence at "The difference between" and therefore adding nothing the disclosure does not already contain), and input/brief.md (used only for formalities and preserved terminology). All 22 claims (1-12 apparatus, 13-17 second apparatus, 18-22 method), all 27 entries of draft/numerals.md, all seven figure briefs with their per-figure numeral lists, the Brief Description of the Drawings, the Summary, the Detailed Description, and the Abstract were read in full and traced limitation by limitation; nothing was sampled.

Ledger result: every limitation, numbered part, structure, relationship, material, result, operating condition, and variant traces to an exact affirmative disclosure passage. Representative traces: rail/flat lower face/upper face/straight longitudinal slot through the rail and printed distance marks beside the slot ("elongated straight rail with a flat lower face... A straight longitudinal slot runs through the rail. Distance marks are printed along the upper face beside the slot"); fixed fence at the first end, perpendicular, downwardly projecting portion bearing on the edge, rail extending inward; reversibility by two screws in two corresponding holes with the same marked upper face reused from an upper or lower edge; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing separation; two separate carriages with lower keys that block rotation but permit sliding; one cylindrical drill bushing per carriage whose bore passes completely through the carriage and registers with an opening through the slot; the two bushing axes parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knob whose shank passes through carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, drawing the shoe toward the carriage to clamp the rail; a pointer on each carriage aligned with its bushing axis and read against the distance marks, whose difference is the center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with that index and with a pencil centerline; the full setting/placing/aligning/drilling/lifting sequence with no part remaining attached; rigid polymer or metal for rail, fence, carriage bodies, shoes, spacer plate, pointers and knobs, hardened-metal replaceable bushings; and the express absence of motor, battery, electronic sensor, and network connection (claims 11 and 22). Dependent-claim limitations (2, 3, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14-17, 19-22) each map to the same passages; no optional embodiment, alternative, or advantage was found that lacks an affirmative source sentence. Background prior-art characterizations were left to the later citation trace, as instructed.

Figure check: the depiction conventions stay inside the figure briefs. "Shown schematically" appears only in figures/FIG-1, FIG-2, FIG-4 and FIG-7 and never in draft/07-drawings.md or draft/08-detailed-description.md; the application text contains no "by way of example," no "any closed outline," and no shape-broadening sentence added to justify a renderer choice. The generic blocks, round knob bodies, plain rectangular fence, elongated slot opening and graduation strokes cover parts the inventor affirmatively disclosed and verbalize no undisclosed depth, taper, angle, runout, radial or circumferential position, or contact topology. The one geometry-bearing statement examined closely, the stepped cutting-plane legs of FIG. 2 lying on the bushing-bore axis and on the clamp-knob axis joined by a lengthwise leg, is compelled by the disclosure, since both the bore's aligned opening and the knob's threaded shank pass through the same single longitudinal slot and must therefore be spaced along it; the brief does not say which lies nearer the fence. Contact statements that are drawn (portion 32 against edge 92, spacer 40 with one face on 32 and the other on 92, shoe below the rail) each restate a disclosure sentence.

Text check: section-line designations are repeated identically in the source view, the resulting view, and the drawing description (3-3 in FIG-2, FIG-3 and 07-drawings; 5-5 in FIG-2, FIG-5 and 07-drawings), and the detailed description repeats both. Every numeral means exactly one thing across the table, the seven figure lists, and the specification; each per-figure numeral list matches the numerals actually called out in that brief with no omission or surplus; every numeral in draft/numerals.md is used in at least one figure; and every parenthetical figure cross-reference in the description (14 in FIG. 4, 12 in FIGS. 3 and 5, 16 and 18 in FIG. 2, 52/54/58/60 in FIG. 5, 72/74/78/80 in FIG. 3, 34/36 in FIG. 6, 24/26/94 in FIG. 7, 40 in FIG. 4, 62/82 in FIG. 2) resolves to a figure that carries that numeral. Claims and description use identical relationships and preserved terms (rail, fixed fence, guide carriage, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, center index, sight notch); antecedent bases and dependencies (5 to 4, 6 to 5, 10 to 9, 14-17 to 13, 19-22 to 18) are sound and single. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains anywhere in the draft. No finding to report.

input.summary:
Full source ledger built and traced. Authority used: input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (truncated mid-sentence at "The difference between", with the remainder duplicated in the disclosure); input/brief.md used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority and no-government-support formalities.

CLAIMS (all 22, three independents 1, 13, 18) were traced limitation by limitation. Rail with flat lower face, upper face, first/second ends, first/second longitudinal sides and a through longitudinal slot carrying distance marks alongside it -> "elongated straight rail with a flat lower face... A straight longitudinal slot runs through the rail. Distance marks are printed along the upper face beside the slot." Fence releasably secured by two screws in two corresponding mounting holes, perpendicular, downwardly projecting portion below the lower face bearing on the straight edge, invertible so that the projecting portion moves to the opposite longitudinal side while the marked upper face still faces away from the workpiece (cls. 1, 8, 16, 20) -> "secured to the first end of the rail by two screws received in two corresponding holes. Removing the screws, turning the fence over, and reinstalling the screws moves the downwardly projecting part... to the opposite longitudinal side. This lets the same marked upper face be used..." Two separately seated carriages, each with a key in the slot that blocks rotation while permitting sliding, one cylindrical drill bushing whose bore passes completely through the carriage and registers with the slot, and a clamp knob whose threaded shank passes through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail that clamps the rail when tightened (cls. 1, 2, 12, 13, 18) -> the corresponding carriage, key, bushing, knob/shank/shoe paragraphs. Parallel bores perpendicular to the flat lower face (cls. 1, 14, 21) -> "The two bushing axes are parallel to one another and perpendicular to the flat lower face." Pointers aligned with bore axes and readable against the marks, difference of readings = center-to-center spacing (cls. 1, 3, 13, 18) -> the pointer paragraph. Center index at midpoint, shallow V sight notch in the second end aligned with it and with the pencil centerline (cls. 4-6, 13, 18) -> the center-index/sight-notch paragraph. Spacer plate with parallel faces increasing setback by its thickness without changing separation (cls. 7, 15, 19) -> the spacer-plate paragraph. Hardened, withdrawable/replaceable bushings and rigid-polymer-or-metal parts (cls. 9, 10, 17) -> the materials paragraph ("replaceable wear parts... hardened metal"). No motor/battery/sensor/network, hand operation, nothing left attached (cls. 11, 22) -> "reusable hand tool", "No part remains attached to the workpiece", "The tool has no motor, battery, electronic sensor, or network connection." Method steps and their order (cl. 18) match the "To use the tool" paragraph exactly.

NUMERALS: all 27 ledger entries (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94) each denote exactly one part, each appears in at least one figure brief, and every parenthetical figure cross-reference in the detailed description (14->FIG. 4, 12->FIG. 3, 16/18->FIG. 2, 52/54/58/60->FIG. 5, 72/74/78/80->FIG. 3, 34/36->FIG. 6, 24/26/94->FIG. 7, 40->FIG. 4) resolves to a brief that actually lists that numeral. No numeral appears in a brief without a ledger entry.

FIGURES: the seven briefs match the Brief Description of the Drawings one-for-one. Section-line designations are repeated identically in the resulting view, the source-view brief and the drawing description: line 3-3 crosses second carriage 70 in FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 is the 3-3 section of carriage 70; line 5-5 crosses first carriage 50 and FIG. 5 is the 5-5 section of carriage 50; the end numerals 3 and 5 and the leftward (toward-fence) viewing arrows are consistent with FIG. 4's stated direction (second end toward first end) and with the fence being at the left/first end in FIGS. 1, 2 and 6. The stepped cutting planes are required by the fact, disclosed in the source, that both the bushing bore and the knob shank pass through the same longitudinal slot and must therefore be offset lengthwise. Generic depictions (plain block carriages, plain round knobs, plain rectangular fence, schematic slot, graduation-line marks, index-line pointers, single-stroke center index, ragged break line) are confined to the figure briefs, are labelled "shown schematically", carry no undisclosed proportion, count, material, taper, depth, angle or contact relationship, and are not echoed or broadened anywhere in the application text; the description and claims remain shape-neutral, and no "by way of example" or "any outline" language appears. Every functional-surface statement present (shoe bearing on the lower face, spacer-plate faces contacting the projecting portion and the edge, projecting portion contacting the edge, key in slot, bore registering with slot, notch in the second end) is verbatim source matter.

TEXT HYGIENE: no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains; the corrective-QA request in input/request.md was treated as non-substantive. Background prior-art characterizations were left for the later citation trace. Abstract is a single paragraph of about 149 words. Claim antecedent bases were checked and are complete.

No unsupported technical assertion and no internal inconsistency was found; findings array is empty.
